dialog.body: Utilities Department, this is Priya. How can I help you?
Hello, yes. Good afternoon. My name is Kathleen McCarthy. I am calling about my water and sewer bill. It is too high again, I think. I do not agree with this one.
Okay, Ms. McCarthy, I can look into that. What's the service address?
288 Malbone Road. North End. I am renter there, but the water bill come to me.
Got it, 288 Malbone Road. Give me a moment to pull up the account. [pause] All right, I have it. What's bothering you about the bill?
The number is high. Much higher than before. I am on fixed income, so I need to make budget. I want breakdown of usage by month. Every month, how much water I use. Can you give me this?
Yes, I can see the readings on the account. Is there a particular stretch you want, like the past year?
Past year, yes. Please. Because I think something is wrong with the reading. I do not use so much water. I live alone.
Okay. I'm looking at it now. The last few billing periods are noticeably higher than the ones from the spring and summer. Has anything changed at the house, any leaks, a running toilet?
Yes, we had plumber come, maybe three weeks ago. The toilet was running. He fixed it. I keep the receipt. It is in my drawer, I have it.

Good, hang on to that. A toilet that runs can add up quickly, so that may explain part of the increase. The plumber's visit would be after some of those high readings, so the next bill should look different.
But I still must pay this one? It is not fair. The toilet is the landlord problem, not mine, and I pay for the water.
I understand. I can't change the charge on the phone, but I can note the account that a repair was made, and you can send in a copy of the receipt. Do you want me to note that?
Yes, please note. I send the receipt. Where I send it?
You can bring it to the utilities counter at City Hall, or I can give you a mailing address. Which is easier for you?
Mail is better. I do not drive now. Please say slowly.
Sure. Address it to the Newport Utilities Department, City Hall, 43 Broadway, Newport, Rhode Island. Put your account address on the receipt, 288 Malbone Road, so we can match it.
Okay, 43 Broadway. I write it down. [pause] Okay. And the monthly breakdown, you mail also?
I can put a usage history together and mail it to the address on the account. Is that the Malbone Road address?
Yes, same. Malbone Road. If you need to call me, my number is 401-555-0189.
Thank you. 401-555-0189, I have that down. It should go out in the mail in the next few days. With the holiday, it may take a little longer to arrive.
Okay, that is fine. One more question. If I want to pay, but City Hall is closed. Can I pay on Saturday? I am not sure how.

City Hall isn't open on Saturdays, but you have options. There's a payment drop box outside the building you can use anytime, you can mail a check, or you can pay online through the city's website at any hour.

Online I do not do so well. My neighbor, the new one, he is next door, he has a flag outside. Red and blue, I do not know this flag. He might help me, but I do not know. Anyway. The drop box, it is okay for check?
Yes, a check in an envelope with your account address written on it works fine in the drop box. Just include the bill stub if you have it.
Okay. I have the stub. I do the check after I get the breakdown. I want to see first.
That makes sense. Just keep an eye on the due date on the bill, so it doesn't go past while you wait for the history.
Yes, the date is January. I have time. But I am annoyed, I tell you honestly. Every time the bill is big, and I am the one who must explain.
I hear you. Once we have the receipt noted and you see the monthly numbers, it should be easier to tell what's going on. If the next reading comes down, that will be a good sign too.
I hope so. Thank you for your help, Miss Priya. Happy holiday.
You're welcome, Ms. McCarthy. Happy holidays to you, and enjoy the rest of your Christmas Eve.
